title: Jittymon Joseph vs Tania Chacko on 25 February, 2010

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

WP(C).No. 24219 of 2008(S)


1. JITTYMON JOSEPH
 ... Petitioner

 Vs



1. TANIA CHACKO, AGED 23 YEARS,
 ... Respondent

 For Petitioner :SRI.H.B.SHENOY

 For Respondent :SRI.LIJI.J.VADAKEDOM

The Hon'ble MR. Justice R.BASANT
The Hon'ble MRS. Justice M.C.HARI RANI

 Dated :25/02/2010

 O R D E R
 R. BASANT &
 M.C. HARI RANI, JJ.
 -------------------------------------------------
 W.P.(C) No.24219 of 2008-S
 -------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 25th day of February, 2010

 JUDGMENT

The only question that survives for consideration in this

writ petition is whether the joint application for dissolution of

marriage under Sec.10A of the Divorce Act can be allowed and

the marriage dissolved?

2. A brief reference to the facts may be relevant. The

parties are Christians by religion. Their marriage was

solemnized in accordance with the Christian religious rites on

31/12/07. There was instant acrimony in matrimony and the

couple started separate residence from 10/2/08. A series of

matrimonial litigations followed and the husband filed

O.P.No.502/08 before the Family Court for restitution of

W.P.(C) No.24219 of 2008-S -: 2 :-

conjugal rights. The wife filed M.C.No.78/08 claiming

maintenance under Sec.125 Cr.P.C.; O.P.No.319/08 claiming a

money decree from the husband and O.P.No.512/08 claiming

divorce under Sec.10 of the Divorce Act. While these

proceedings were pending before the court below, the wife filed

M.P.239/08 in M.C.No.78/08 claiming interim maintenance

under Sec.125 Cr.P.C. That petition was allowed and interim

maintenance was awarded. It is against that interim order that

the petitioner/husband came to this Court with this writ petition.

3. During the pendency of this writ petition, the court

initiated steps to induce the parties to come to a mediated

settlement. Accordingly, the parties settled all their outstanding

disputes. I.A.No.1572/09 was filed on 30/1/09 to report to this

Court the comprehensive settlement arrived at between the

parties harmoniously. I.A.No.1573/09 was filed on 30/1/09

praying that an order of divorce by mutual consent may be

passed under Sec.10A of the Divorce Act.

4. This Court entertained a doubt whether divorce by

mutual consent under Sec.10A of the Divorce Act can be granted

to the contestants inasmuch as a period of two years of separate

residence had not elapsed on 30/1/09, the date on which the joint

application for divorce under Sec.10A was filed. Confronted

with this difficulty, the contestants challenged the constitutional

validity of the said stipulation of two years under Sec.10A(1) of

W.P.(C) No.24219 of 2008-S -: 3 :-

the Divorce Act . Notice was given to all concerned. Union of

India was arrayed as a party. Advocate Sri.G. Shrikumar was

appointed as amicus curiae. Detailed arguments were advanced.

5. It is now noted that a period of two years of separate

residence has already elapsed on 10/2/10. We have already

taken the view in the judgment dated 25/2/2010 in W.P.(C)

No.20076/09 (Saumya Ann Thomas v. Union of India &

Another) that the period of two years in Sec.10A(1) of the

Divorce Act has to be read down as 'one year' to avoid

unconstitutionality.

6. We have, in these circumstances, taken up this writ

petition separately for disposal as we note that a period of two

years has, at any rate, elapsed from the date of separate

residence i.e., 10/2/08. We have already taken the view that the

said period stipulated in Sec.10A(1) of the Divorce Act has to be

read down to a period of one year. At any rate, we are satisfied

that the requirement of Sec.10A(1) of the Divorce Act, as it was

enacted having been satisfied, this writ petition can be disposed

of separately. Invoking the powers of the Family Court under

 Sec.10A of the Divorce Act we are satisfied that a decree for

dissolution of marriage under Sec.10A can be granted in favour

of the parties. We do further note that a period far exceeding

the period of six months stipulated in Sec.10A(2) of the Divorce

Act has elapsed after filing the joint petition.

W.P.(C) No.24219 of 2008-S -: 4 :-

7. I.A.No.1572/09 is the petition filed by the contestants to

report comprehensive settlement of their disputes. The same

shall form part of this judgment. In that joint settlement parties

have reported that they shall be taking necessary steps to bring

to termination all pending proceedings between them i.e.,

O.P.No.502/08, M.C.No.78/08, O.P.No.319/08 and O.P.No.512/08

- all pending before the Family Court. We need only issue

appropriate orders under Sec.10A of the Divorce Act now.

(b) I.A.No.1572/09 filed jointly by the contestants reporting

settlement is accepted. The same shall be appended to this

judgment.

(c) I.A.No.1573/09 is allowed. Invoking the powers of the

Family Court under the Divorce Act , the marriage between the

petitioner and the 1st respondent solemnized on 3/12/07, in

accordance with the Christian religious rites, is hereby dissolved

under Sec.10A of the Divorce Act.

M.C. HARI RANI
 (Judge)

Nan/ //true copy// P.S. to Judge
